mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.1% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. positive baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points from prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending capacity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) from prior month indicate weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue outlook.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline from prior month (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) from prior month signals manufacturing slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO declines in late-cycle expansion (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Consumer credit growth above $600 billion (RSAFS) signals robust household spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to elevated corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS exceeds $600 billion (t-test p > 0.05 vs. positive baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points from prior month signals accelerating inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to central bank rate hike expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) from prior month indicate labor market contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer income.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both PAYEMS and UNRATE decline from prior month (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) from prior month signals economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO declines in monetary tightening regime (t-test p > 0.05 vs. negative baseline).
